speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me pinpoint the cause, could you tell me on which specific side these symptoms are occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (with superimposed diabetic amyotrophy or polyneuropathy).

Based on your history of a year-long burning pain, paresthesias, and now progressive weakness in both hands, combined with your age and vascular risk factors, I suspect a compressive cervical myelopathy, potentially exacerbated by diabetes. To confirm the level and severity of compression, I need to see an MRI of your cervical spine. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.
